title: Chapter 91
content:
Pedal to the metal, the sedan screeched through the deluge, but Takeya Jun’s car clung to their rear bumper like a heat-seeking missile.

Wang Han fumbled with his phone, frantically punching in Park Tae-soo’s direct line. The call connected on the very first ring, and Han roared into the receiver:

"Chief Park! We're taking heavy fire! Scramble backup to our route immediately!"

Before he could demand heavy ordnance, SLAM!

The concussive rear impact violently pitched the chassis, sending the phone clattering onto the floorboards. As Han bent to retrieve it, Jun’s sedan rammed them a second time. Han’s head whipped forward, smashing hard against the dashboard.

He groaned in agony, clutching his bleeding forehead, while Jakyeong stomped the accelerator to the firewall.

The gap refused to widen. Rolling his driver’s side window down, Jun hung out of the frame, emptying magazine after magazine into their flank with relentless precision.

Jakyeong and Han ducked beneath the dash as rounds perforated the upholstery. The front windshield spiderwebbed and caved in, letting the torrential downpour flood straight into their faces.

Fuck. Blown windshield, zero visibility, and an unrelenting hail of lead.

They had to hold out and buy time. Given Kang Il-hyun’s psychotic possessiveness, an encrypted GPS tracker was undoubtedly hardwired into their chassis. All they could do was pray the cavalry breached the perimeter before their luck ran out.

After thirty grueling minutes of high-speed evasive maneuvering, the storm abruptly broke, the rain giving way to a humid, gray haze.

As they crossed a long bridge over a swollen river, a stray round found their rear axle.

BANG.

The left rear tire shredded into airborne rubber. The sedan spun violently out of control, tires screaming across the slick asphalt. Jakyeong counter-steered with all his might, pumping the brakes, but the standing rainwater negated all traction.

With a deafening CRASH, the car slammed sideways into the bridge's concrete parapet.

The airbags detonated with explosive force, snapping Jakyeong and Han back into their headrests.

Fighting through the ringing shock, Jakyeong glanced at the cracked side mirror.

VROOOM—!

Jun’s engine roared as the black sedan aligned its nose, preparing to ram them straight through the shattered guardrail and into the abyss.

"Out! Now!"

Jakyeong ripped off his seatbelt, kicking the driver's door wide and hauling Han out onto the wet asphalt.

A split second later, Jun’s car plowed into their ruined sedan with terrifying momentum. The collision pulverized the concrete barrier, launching the vehicle over the ledge to plunge into the churning river below.

Jun brought his car to a halt, stepping onto the pavement as he racked a fresh magazine into his sidearm. Even in the sweltering midsummer heat, he wore a battered black leather jacket. A jagged, faded scar cut from the corner of his lip across his cheekbone—a souvenir carved by his own parents decades ago, whom he had subsequently slaughtered with his bare hands.

Leaning lazily against his warm hood, Jun surveyed the two unarmed operatives.

"Long time, Wei."

That sneering, razor-thin smirk was the last thing Jakyeong ever wanted to see. Forcing a tight, venomous grin, Jakyeong replied:

"Long time indeed, aniki. Life seems to be treating you remarkably well."

"I've heard the rumors," Jun purred, his eyes raking over Jakyeong with filthy condescension. "Word on the street is you've taken quite a liking to men lately. Opening your legs for some rich patron, are you?"

Jakyeong’s face darkened instantly.

Han stepped forward, putting an arm out to shield his younger brother. "Jun, stop this. Wei was your partner. You practically raised him in the trade."

"Partner?" Jun scoffed, letting out a sharp, derisive bark of laughter. "A spineless, sentimental weakling like him?"

Jakyeong cast a discreet glance over the fractured ledge. The river below was running fast and violent from the storm. Surviving the drop was mathematically possible, but taking a bullet in the back on the way down was a certainty.

He shifted his weight, preparing to body-check Han over the railing first to give his brother a fighting chance.

Jun caught the subtle muscle twitch instantly, shifting his suppressed muzzle directly onto Wang Han's forehead.

"Don't try it, Wei. Not with me."

Jakyeong locked eyes with the barrel. "Take my head and let him walk. Han has nothing to do with this ledger."

Jun broke into a wet, psychotic giggle—a shrill, manic sound that made the hairs on Jakyeong's arms stand on end.

"Always the same. A butcher who insists on playing the righteous martyr."

He was dredging up Macau. Years ago, on a joint contract, Jun had abducted the six-year-old son of a high-ranking defector, intending to dismember the child piece by piece and mail the parts to the parents to force their surrender. Jakyeong had covertly severed the boy's zip-ties and facilitated his escape, blowing the entire multimillion-dollar operation.

Han bowed his head, his tone low and diplomatic. "Let Wei go, Jun. Whatever debt is owed, I will clear it out of my own pocket."

"Shut the fuck up, both of you," Jun spat, waving the gun in a lazy arc between them. "I'm putting two in the dirt today. The only question is whose skull I crack open first."

Jakyeong inched backward, his heel brushing the shattered edge of the bridge. Han subtly mirrored his footing.

On three, we dive together.

Just as Jakyeong gathered the tension in his thighs—

ROOOOAAAR—!

The deafening wail of a twin-turbo V8 ruptured the quiet.

Crossing the median at over a hundred miles an hour, a reinforced black executive sedan struck Takeya Jun like a freight train.

THUD.

The impact launched Jun's body ten feet into the air like a ragdoll before slamming hard against the asphalt, rolling several times before coming to a dead stop.

Jakyeong stood frozen with his hands on the concrete parapet. Han stared in stunned silence.

Jun lay motionless in a pool of rainwater, entirely unconscious.

The doors of the black sedan swung open, and Kang Il-hyun and Park Tae-soo stepped out.

Ignoring the crumpled hitman on the pavement, Il-hyun marched straight toward Jakyeong, his dark, ravenous eyes conducting a frantic, head-to-toe inventory.

"Are you hurt?"

Jakyeong blinked, nodding dumbly. I never imagined he'd drive the intercept vehicle himself.

Il-hyun reached into his tailored jacket, drawing a spare automatic sidearm and tossing it across. Jakyeong caught it out of the air by the grip.

Il-hyun’s lips pulled into an amused, mocking smirk. "Can't act to save your life, and now you're leaving your weapons behind like an amateur?"

Jakyeong racked the slide, looking away in sheepish embarrassment.

Il-hyun glanced back at his security chief. "Tae-soo. Isn't this technically gross breach of contract? Shouldn't we sue our lead operative for criminal fraud?"

As Jakyeong raised the weapon to put a bullet through Jun’s skull, Tae-soo moved in first, hauling the unconscious hitman up by the collar to drag him toward the trunk. In the scuffle, the leather jacket shifted, exposing the bare skin between Jun's shoulder blades.

Il-hyun’s eyes snagged on the ink. He strode over, yanking the shirt down.

Carved across Jun’s shoulder was an identical, coiled black serpent—the exact same tattoo branded across Lee Ja-kyeong.

The temperature on the bridge plunged to absolute zero. Il-hyun's gaze sharpened into pure, murderous malice.

In that fraction of a second, the 'unconscious' Jun flicked his wrist. A spring-loaded combat blade snapped from his sleeve, slashing in a blinding arc aimed straight for Il-hyun's jugular.

Il-hyun’s left hand caught the wrist mid-air with bone-crushing force.

The blade clattered to the asphalt. Without breaking momentum, Il-hyun wrenched the arm backward, twisting the joint past its anatomical limit.

CRACK.

A sickening snap echoed over the water as the radius and ulna tore through the skin in a compound fracture.

Jun unleashed a bloodcurdling shriek of agony, collapsing forward as he clutched the mangled limb.

Il-hyun sank into a casual crouch before the thrashing hitman. Reaching out, he buried a fist into Jun’s hair, wrenching the man's head back to force their eyes to lock.

"What is your relationship with Lee Ja-kyeong?"

Even as sweat and agony poured down his face, Jun cradled his ruined wrist and let out a broken, wheezing cackle.

"Curious... are you?"

Behind them, Jakyeong closed his eyes in exasperation. Shut your mouth. Say one more word and you're a dead man.

But Takeya Jun was a suicidal degenerate.

"We go way back," Jun wheezed, glaring mockingly at Jakyeong. "Intimate history. Isn't that right, Wei?"

Jun’s gaze locked onto Jakyeong, and Il-hyun slowly turned his head to follow the line of sight.

Trapped beneath the heavy, suffocating weight of both men's stares, Jakyeong’s jaw twitched in indignant fury.

Il-hyun’s face fell into a wounded, tragic pout.

"Darling... you swore I was your very first man."

The cadence was identical to the night he swung a woodchopping axe into a man's skull. Jakyeong desperately shook his head in frantic denial, but Jun wasn't finished digging his own grave.

"How does his ass taste?" Jun mocked, spitting blood. "Devastating, isn't it?"

Il-hyun’s gaze drifted slowly back down to Jun.

An identical serpent tattoo. The exact same trade. Fucking disgusting.

"Do not look at me with those arrogant eyes," Il-hyun whispered softly.

Jun spat a bloody laugh. "Why? Gonna gouge my fucking eyes out—"

Before the sentence cleared his teeth, Il-hyun clamped his right palm over Jun’s face.

His left thumb plunged with terrifying velocity straight beneath the lower lid of Jun's right eye socket.

Jun spasmed violently, a muffled, horrifying shriek tearing from his throat. Tae-soo locked the hitman's shoulders down from behind, holding the thrashing body rigid.

Il-hyun drove his finger deeper into the orbital bone, hooked the optic nerve, and ripped the wet, glistening eyeball clean out of the skull.

An agonized, inhuman scream shattered the air as Jun’s limbs violently convulsed. Standing a few paces back, Jakyeong watched in dead, frozen silence as crimson poured down the man's shredded cheek.

Il-hyun clamped his fingers around Jun's jaw, forcing the bloody face upright.

Dangling the severed right eye inches from Jun's remaining left pupil, Il-hyun flashed a bright, demonic smile.

"Say hello. Meet your right eye."

Jun trembled from head to toe, the unmasked arrogance in his remaining eye dissolving into pure, paralyzing terror.

"Repeat what you said earlier," Il-hyun purred, his voice dropping into a lethal register.

"..."

"Tell me again how Lee Ja-kyeong tasted."

When no answer came, Il-hyun closed his fist, crushing the eyeball like a ripe grape.

Vitreous fluid and dark blood splattered across Il-hyun’s cheek. He ran two fingers through the gore on his face, brought it to his tongue to taste the iron, and spat it onto the pavement with a look of mild disgust.

"Tastes remarkably bland for an eyeball."

Jun hung in Tae-soo's grip, trembling uncontrollably, his remaining pupil pinned to the ground in sheer, unadulterated horror. A monster. This man is a literal demon from hell.

"I asked you a question," Il-hyun murmured, leaning in. "Or would you prefer I scoop out the left one as well?"

"..."

"Curious to know what it feels like to spend the rest of your pathetic life hunted in absolute darkness?"

"Stop it!" Jakyeong barked, stepping forward.

Il-hyun rose to his full height. Taking in the bloody, pulverized pulp dripping from his fingers, Jakyeong felt a cold shudder crawl down his spine. Eye gouging... the man has completely lost his mind.

"There is nothing between us!" Jakyeong yelled, frantic. "He's just an old operational contact from years ago!"

Il-hyun pulled a silk handkerchief from his breast pocket, meticulously wiping the blood and fluid from his skin. A tender, dazzling smile returned to his handsome face.

"We will confirm the fine details once we get home, darling."

The words were wrapped in honey, but the temperature behind them was arctic. Il-hyun gave Tae-soo a curt nod, instructing him to secure Jun in the trunk. Tae-soo shoved the groaning, half-blind hitman into the cargo bay and slammed the lid.

Jakyeong rushed to Il-hyun's side, pleading his case over and over—demanding he just put a bullet in Jun's head and bury him on the riverbank right now.

His protests were entirely ignored. Jakyeong and Wang Han were firmly ushered into the rear leather seats of the armored sedan, placed under direct executive escort back to the estate.

The thirty-minute drive was suffocatingly quiet. If Wang Ryun had been present, he would have cracked a tasteless joke to break the ice; today, his loud mouth was sorely missed.

As the car cleared the gates of the estate, Il-hyun finally broke the dead silence.

"Tae-soo."

"Yes, President Kang."

"Are you proficient at filleting sashimi?"

"I trained under a master chef in my youth, sir."

Sashimi? In this mood? Does he want to stop for raw fish right now?

Il-hyun’s next words shattered that assumption into dust.

"Splendid. Then you can skin the serpent tattoo straight off Lee Ja-kyeong’s back."

Jakyeong’s head snapped toward the rearview mirror, his eyes blowing wide in horror.

"What did you just say?!"

Il-hyun ignored him completely, staring out the front windshield in serene, unbothered silence.

Filleting? Skinning? What am I, a fucking sea bass?!

Jakyeong opened his mouth to rage, only for Il-hyun to cut him off with a chilling, single-sentence ultimatum:

"Shut your mouth and sit quietly, darling... before I decide to handle the knife myself."
